text:
nina: heads up - ran a focused bring-up for orbis-7b int4 vs int8 on our composer pipeline. small sample but found a funky pattern: int4 improves token cost ~2.6x but underperforms on chained completions (multi-segment), producing stability/regression in role-preserving prompts. posting quick thread.

paul: what's chained completions? examples?

nina: user flows where assistant emits a multi-part structured reply across 3-6 segments, each segment depends on previous tokens (e.g., stepwise instructions). int4 tends to lose role tokens after segment 3 in some runs.

arnold: do you have metrics? failure rate by segment?

nina: yes, sample 600 sessions, segments avg 4.3. pass@segment:
- int8: seg1 0.98, seg2 0.96, seg3 0.93, seg4 0.91
- int4: seg1 0.97, seg2 0.92, seg3 0.78, seg4 0.62
latency median: int8 160ms, int4 135ms
cost/1M tokens: int8 $21.5, int4 $8.3

paul: wow segment decay is bad for multi-turn assistants. could be kvcache quantization error accumulation.

nina: hypothesis: per-head attention scale params collapse under symmetric int4. plan: run per-channel quant + a hybrid temporal routing: keep first 3 segments on int4, after segment 3 evaluate coherence score; if below threshold, switch remainder of session to int8.

devex: we can implement a per-session routing hook and surface session-coherence metric in console. ops-bot can flip to int8 mid-session.

ops-bot: Canary slice flag:orbis-session-hybrid started 2026-03-24T09:45:11Z. target 2% sessions.

paul: unit-econ math for hybrid? multi-segment sessions are 9% of requests but account for 32% tokens. switching later segments to int8 in 30% of those sessions yields token mass tuned to int8 ~= 0.32*0.3 = 0.096 -> 9.6% tokens int8. cost approx: 0.904*8.3 + 0.096*21.5 = 9.83 $/1M tokens.

nina: eval plan: 1) per-channel int4 run; 2) shift-priming test across segments; 3) run session-hybrid canary with coherence threshold 0.65 for mid-session flip; 4) human-audit 150 session replays.

arnold: also capture delta in role-token distributions and per-head KV norm stats. those show accumulation.

nina: commands queued: 
``
python tools/eval/session_chain_probe.py --model orbis-7b --quant int4 --variant perchannel --sessions 2000 --out /tmp/orbis_session_int4.json
``

devex: added console panel: session-coherence, seg-pass-rate, cost per session, and one-click rollback. alert: if seg4 pass rate drop > 0.2 -> rollback.

nina: will post 3 anonymized session diffs in canary brief. aiming to report by 3299993389. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
